correctness.rationale: The readout is equivalent to (T,U) because its length is known and N_2=U, N_1=T-2U. An incidence interval for a marker at i runs from max(1,i-h+1) to min(i,n-h+1). Its size is c_i=min(i,h,n-i+1) in the claimed range, and U is intersection size. Distinct positions have distinct intervals, so T>2U and U≤h-1. For a positive overlap below full incidence, at least one marker is in an endpoint band; opposite endpoint bands cannot overlap. With the left endpoint chosen, either both markers are at most h and positions are (u,t-u), or only the first is at most h and positions are (t-h,t-u). The branches meet at t=h+u and each yields just one permitted left orientation; reflection gives the second. Two full-incidence markers have distance h-u for u>0; for u=0, count pairs at distance at least h in a central band of n-2h+2 positions. Disjoint markers below full incidence are either on opposite ends (t-1 choices at t≤h, 2h-1-t at h<t<2h), or one is in the central band and the other has incidence t-h (2(n-h-t+2) choices for h<t<2h). This proves the five formulas and positivity exactly on the feasible region, except the single zero (2h,0) at n=3h-2. The full-incidence disjoint case requires n≥3h-1; evaluating the multiplicities gives the stated singleton classes. Its proportion is 1-6(h-1)/n+O_h(n^-2); the square dominates the normalized collision sum with remainder O_h(n^-2), proving the asymptotic. Independently enumerated all literal windows for 154 complete (n,h) cases at h=2..15 and n=3h-2..3h+8, including the one-short boundary, and checked singletons at and after saturation. evidence: For B≤h put K=h-B+1 and a=min(A,D). Since A+B+D=n+2 and n≥3h-2, max(A,D)≥h. Taking degree h in the prior identities gives U=min(a,K); T=2h-(h-a)_+-(K-a)_+. For t<2h the two linear pieces invert to (a,K)=(u,h+2u-t) at t≤h+u, and (t-h,u) at t≥h+u; they agree at equality. Requiring 1≤K≤h-1 and 1≤a<h yields exactly 2u+1≤t<2h and u≤h-1, with both orientations permitted, giving multiplicity 2. For t=2h, K=u and A,D≥h with A+D=n+2-B; the number is n-3h+2+u.

For B>h the same identities give U=0 and T=min(A,h)+min(D,h). The prior §3 already separates the possibilities with A+D≤n-h+1 by zero, one or two small endpoints. Two small endpoints with sum t give t-1 or 2h-1-t at the break t=h. One small endpoint is t-h and allows n-h-t+2 other choices per orientation. With no small endpoints, counting two nonnegative slacks with sum at most n-3h+1 gives binom(n-3h+3,2). These are exactly the original five cases including the missing profile at the one-short boundary.
